Dungeon Run
Endless waves — pick a weapon and a difficulty
The run you know. Choose a weapon, a squad and a difficulty from Normal all the way up to Professional, then survive as many waves as you can. Levels, crates, drops, iCoins — everything is earned in here.
PLAY
Boss Battles
One fight, one enemy, no waves
Step into a bare arena against a single boss built to be fought at your ceiling. No waves and nothing to pick up — you arrive with your weapon at its maximum level and your character at level 40, and the boss pays its purse only if you kill it.

BOSS BATTLES

Corrupted Chronarch
10,000,000 HP · the time-lord, rotted through · LV 85 · 750 iCoins to enter
The Chronarch as it becomes when the time it steals starts eating it back. Half again the size, ten million health, and every projectile it throws travels more than three times as fast as the ones you have learned to read — thrown 40% more often, and shredding three points of any shield for every one they soak. It does not spray attacks at random: it winds up in full view, commits to ONE move, then leaves you a window. A CLOCKWORK SWARM of ten rotating volleys you walk the gaps of. A DESTRUCTIVE REWIND that swallows most of the arena and mends the boss while it burns you. A barrage of expanding lances that bloom into chronospheres. Between them it opens a TEMPORAL TOME to heal itself, shoves you off at close range, throws three staggered TIME SLASHES you can only dash through, and hauls you back if you run past 31 tiles. There are no waves and nothing to pick up — you enter at maximum weapon level and character level 40, with every level-up package that brings. Everything it throws is a percentage of your max HP, so the pattern is what kills you, not your build. Opens at Account Level 85 and costs 750 iCoins per attempt — a retry stakes another 750. Kill it and it pays 7,500 account points and 1,000 iCoins.
ENTER
Corrupted Mech
10,000,000 HP · half again as big, and it never stops chasing · LV 85 · 750 iCoins to enter
The armoured colossus, corrupted. It keeps the whole Warmachine kit — the homing BURN stream, the charged PLASMA BOMB it winds up in full view, the reflecting shockwave shield it channels at 66% and 33%, and the lane volleys that sweep the arena from edge to edge — but every one of those timers comes round a QUARTER sooner, so the gaps you learned on the ordinary Mech are not there any more. The wind-ups themselves are untouched: the telegraphs are still readable, there is just less breathing room between them. From HALF HEALTH down it also starts calling FIRE PILLARS across the whole arena on the same one-second cadence the Flamethrower's own pillars use — three to five at a time, every one of them marked on the ground for a full second before the column drops, so the wind-up is the fight. It is also HALF AGAIN AS BIG, and it throws STALKERS: single homing embers, one every couple of seconds, each slower than you can run but incapable of turning away. Any one of them is outrunnable; four of them on the field at once means the thing that kills you is standing still to shoot. And it fights ALONE — the corrupted one has no Fire drones to deploy and nothing to hide behind, so the only thing in the arena is the thing shooting at you. It takes no knockback at all — but it DEALS it: the burn rounds nudge, a stalker hits like a truck, the plasma bomb launches you, and the full overload throws you across the arena. Ten million health, no waves, nothing to pick up: you arrive at maximum weapon level and character level 40. Opens at Account Level 85 and costs 750 iCoins per attempt — a retry stakes another 750. Kill it and it pays 7,500 account points and 1,000 iCoins.
ENTER
The Still Storm
120,000,000 HP · the storm colossus · LV 150 · 2,000 iCoins to enter
A storm-golem left standing where a city used to be. It is a GROUND fight: seven tiles of crackling lightning in the shape of a person, walking at you the whole time, with a shadow under it and the floor ringing at every footfall. Everything it throws SHOVES you, and the shove is part of the attack: a storm wall pushes you along its own travel, a thunder stomp throws you out with its ring, a blast launches you. PHASE 1: a spaced loop, one thing at a time — a STORM WALL sweeping the arena with one marked gap to dash through, CLOUD-TO-GROUND strikes on telegraphed circles, and a STATIC BURST of six slow orbs. PHASE 2 at 75%: it closes the distance and its beats stop queueing — they land TOGETHER, a PINCER of two moves arriving from different angles on the same frame — a DOUBLE STORM WALL from both sides with a single shared gap that DETONATES if the walls meet with you outside it, an ARC CAGE of eight rods slammed into the ground around you that chain to each other (one rod is always missing — that gap is the way out), and PRECISION STRIKES zigzagging onto you. At exactly 40% everything stops: it freezes dead for two full seconds, then a pillar of lightning stands in the arena and PULSES — the gaps between pulses are the only way through. PHASE 3, the Silent Storm: OVERLAPPING WAVES with barely a quarter-second between them — nothing waits for anything else, and two or three attacks are live at once from the first beat — an ORBITAL STORM dropped on your head, a THUNDER STOMP that sends three rings out across the ground for you to outrun, FURY STRIKES with no safe ground, and THE STILL STORM'S WRATH, a beam that turns twice all the way round. Kill it and it stops dead, holds for a second and a half, and then the loudest thunderclap in the game breaks over the arena. Opens at Account Level 150 and costs 2,000 iCoins per attempt. It pays 12,000 account points, 5,000 iCoins and a WEEKLY BOSS CHEST (the chest once per week).
ENTER
The Castellan & The Warden
75,000,000 HP each · neither falls alone · LV 160 · 2,500 iCoins to enter
Two bodies, one fight. The CASTELLAN is a bluish-white being that holds its distance, mends its partner and throws light; the WARDEN is a dark knight in a closed helm whose whole book is about distance and taking it away from you. Its CLEAVE lands on the angle it committed to when it raised the blade, so it can be stepped round — but the blade comes straight back the other way a quarter-second later as a RIPOSTE, wider and with no wind-up, and walking out of the first arc walks you into the second. Out at range it throws THE CHAIN OF JUDGMENT, a hook on twelve tiles of iron that drags whatever it catches back to the knight while it is already swinging. Up close it plants and turns: THE WARDEN'S WHEEL, a second and a half of spinning blade that owns four tiles of ground and walks at you the whole time. And it still CHARGES the length of the arena and lands in a shockwave. Neither can be killed alone: whichever falls first is DOWNED and spends EIGHT SECONDS hauling ITSELF back up, needing nobody, which means putting one down never takes the other off you. Worse, it does not come back the same: every rising puts it back on FULL health — the whole of its new, larger pool — with +25% MAX HEALTH, +25% DEFENSE and +75% ATTACK SPEED on top of what it already had, and it stacks every time — so the fight is won only by putting both down inside the same window. While they are within ten tiles they are BONDED and 60% of everything you land on one is paid by the other, which is why they spend the fight walking apart, and why forcing them together is the whole game. And with its partner on the floor the knight takes THE BLACK VOW: it goes dark and hot, every clock it owns runs 30% faster, everything it lands hits 25% harder, and every hit it puts on you shaves 0.4s off the clock on the floor — up to three whole seconds, so the eight you bought is only as long as your footwork. The Castellan's ward halves damage inside it. Stalling does not wear them down, it arms them — a fight you cannot close inside those eight seconds is a fight against a pair that keeps rising harder than it fell.
ENTER
Mutated Chronarch
65,000,000 HP · what the rot mutated it into · LV 175 · 4,000 iCoins to enter
The corrupted one mutated past saving. Sixty-five million health, the same scripted loop, the same lances and slashes and falling sky. Its CLOCKBURST opens SLOW and doubles every phase: a quarter tempo while it is healthy, half at two thirds, and full speed for the last third — the same shape you learned at the start, arriving four times as fast by the end. Each ring is twisted differently so the gaps never line up, and it chains three casts back to back. TIME HAIL is its alone: the ordinary Chronarch bolt hosed 55 times in under three seconds, two and a half times its usual speed, each one leaning very slightly toward you so a lazy dodge is not enough. And it throws a TIME RELIC somewhere at random — a blue shockwave rolls out from wherever it lands so you can find it, and a thirty-second clock sits over its head. Break it or it kills you outright: no defence, no absorb, no dodge, no shield. Its chronospheres open with NO WIND-UP, and its leash sits 15% further out. In exchange the TOME stays shut and only opens when you push it into a NEW PHASE. Opens at Account Level 175 and costs 4,000 iCoins per attempt — a retry stakes another 4,000. Kill it and it pays 20,000 account points, 10,000 iCoins and 7 Temporal Crates.
ENTER
Abyssal Warmachine
700,000,000 HP · LV 190 · 12,000 iCoins to enter
The Mutated Warmachine with the last of it burned out: more than eight times the health, the whole mutated kit, and an OVERLOAD SHIELD that is no longer a damage check. It holds for TWENTY-FOUR seconds, and across those seconds it runs EIGHT three-second cycles. Each cycle opens a thin RING somewhere around it, tolls the curse, then strikes twice — a blaze, then a lower blaze. On the third beat everything outside that ring is annihilated. Not damaged: gone. The ring is the only ground there is, it moves every cycle, and you still have to break the shield on hits while you are being herded around it.

Mutated Warmachine
85,000,000 HP · the rot went all the way through · LV 180 · 5,000 iCoins to enter
The Corrupted Mech with nothing left holding it together. Eighty-five million health, every timer a quarter faster, and the whole corrupted kit — the burn bursts, the charged plasma bomb, the lane volleys, the fire pillars. Two things are its alone. THE OVERLOAD SHIELD no longer waits for two thirds health: it goes up the moment the fight starts and again at the top of EVERY phase, it holds for FIFTEEN SECONDS, and it is not broken by big hits but by MANY — TWO HUNDRED of them in the first phase, three hundred in the second and four hundred in the third, whatever they are worth, so a fast weapon breaks it and a heavy one does not. Break it in time and the overload comes out as a shove and nothing more. Fail and it comes out ARENA-WIDE and takes most of you with it, wherever you were standing. A curse tolls once a second while it holds, and climbs in pitch as the window closes. And INCINERATE: it stops dead, everything holstered, and holds a low hum — then a beam of fire opens out of it and SWEEPS, turning toward you the whole time it burns. It cannot be outrun in a straight line, only cut across. While the beam is out it goes back to fighting with everything else at once; only the hum buys you a free moment.

⬢ The Armoury

Everything you can equip or consume, in one grid. Relics slot in, elements and weapon variants are consumed to unlock them for good. Anything still darkened has not been found yet — click it and it will tell you so.

∑ Equation Shards

Rare materials that drop off anything you kill. You never spend them — every shard you have ever picked up buffs its stat by a tiny amount permanently, across every run you will ever play. Each one is almost nothing on its own; a few thousand is not.

🎨 Player Colors

INFO & CONTROLS

HOW TO PLAY

You're dropped into an endless arena and the goal is simple: survive. Pick a weapon, then move with WASD (or the arrow keys), aim with your mouse, and hold or click to fire. Enemies pour in wave after wave, and each one you kill drops XP. Collect enough and you level up mid-run, which lets you pick a buff — more damage, faster attacks, extra defense, life steal, whatever fits your build. There's no single "right" choice; part of the fun is stacking buffs that turn your weapon into something ridiculous.

The longer you last, the nastier it gets. Tougher enemies and minibosses show up every 5 waves as you climb, and at wave 50 the time-lord Chronarch — a true multi-phase boss — arrives. Keep moving, use your dash to slip out of bad spots, and don't get greedy chasing kills into a corner. When you eventually go down, the iCoins you earned that run are yours to keep — spend them in the iCoin Shop on permanent upgrades and unlocks that make your next run stronger. Minibosses can even drop rare crates containing weapon skins. Die, upgrade, and come back harder. That's the loop.

CONTROLS

WASD / Arrows: Move

Mouse: Aim

Click: Attack

Z: Weapon Ability (when your weapon has one) or Dash

Dash, Ability, and Game Speed keys can be changed in Settings → Keybinds
